source.title: On the Selection of Initialization and Activation Function for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Soufiane Hayou; A. Doucet; J. Rousseau

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including supplementary theoretical and experimental sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares random initializations and activation functions and reports their effects on learning speed and test accuracy, using MNIST rather than the versions’ training-error measure.
record.gate_note: The empirical results measure validation or test accuracy and learning speed, not training classification error. The paper’s theoretical results and cited findings are not recorded as result rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 in fully connected Swish networks on MNIST: changing random initialization relative to the edge of chaos changes learning curves and whether deeper networks learn successfully. V4 concerns learning speed and trainable depth, so training classification error is not required. This study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors show that edge-of-chaos initialization improves information propagation, while ReLU correlations still collapse polynomially with depth. They give sufficient activation conditions for slower collapse, identify Swish as a candidate, and report MNIST learning benefits from edge-of-chaos initialization and Swish, especially at greater depth.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use Adam on MNIST and compare random initializations and activations using validation/test accuracy and learning curves; they do not measure the versions’ training-error outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization choice relative to the edge of chaos; activation function; network depth and width.

fits_no_version.finding: Tanh learns faster than ReLU at depth 5 but stalls at low accuracy at depth 40 or greater, attributed to small gradients.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice changes learning speed and usable depth in fully connected MNIST networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Swish generally outperforms ReLU, especially in deeper architectures; ReLU has slightly higher validation accuracy in the two smallest tested architectures with depth exceeding width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Swish's learning and held-out accuracy advantages over ReLU depend on network depth and width.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says the Python code to reproduce experiments will be made available on-line.
record.peer_reviewed: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2019; venue listed as arXiv.org.
record.problems: Experiments report validation/test accuracy rather than training classification error. Numerical learning-curve values are not reported in the text. The paper says the Gaussian-process approximation is inaccurate when depth exceeds width, and Table 3 does not state the dataset in its caption or surrounding text.
record.rows_left_out: None. All separately reported Table 2 and Table 3 activation-by-architecture accuracy results and the described Figure 5–7 comparisons are recorded.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and additional student neurons.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified deep plain tanh and Fixup results.

Orthogonal versus same-variance Gaussian initialization, orthogonal convolution kernels, and training 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks. Learning speed here is assessed through held-out accuracy curves rather than training loss or training error.
Stability thresholds, curvature evolution, loss recovery above the threshold, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Theoretical initialization results underlying V4's signal-propagation mechanism: ReLU edge-of-chaos initialization preserves variance, but correlations still approach 1 with 1-c_l asymptotic to 9π²/(2l²). For qualifying activations, reducing bias variance along the edge of chaos makes the correlation map approach the identity. These are infinite-width propagation results, not measured training-speed endpoints.

record.verdict_notes: The activation comparisons do not justify the record's V4 limits_scope label: V4 does not claim that Swish uniformly beats ReLU. The supplied text contains figure captions and qualitative descriptions but no readable plotted curves, so exact initialization-specific endpoints and effect sizes cannot be verified.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the listed model-size and stopping conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Plain versus residual convolutional networks, batch normalization, and shortcut effects. The paper discusses depth and activation effects in fully connected networks but does not test the version’s shortcut comparison.

The paper does not test orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, convolutional networks, or 10,000-layer networks. Its experiments use MNIST and compare edge-of-chaos initialization, activation functions, and fully connected network depths and widths.
Learning rates above the stability limit, curvature or sharpness, loss recovery, and divergence.
Batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

relationships.condition: MNIST fully connected Swish networks, Figure 5: width 30/depth 20 and width 80/depth 40, Adam with learning rate 0.001
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 compare initialization-dependent learning curves; the text reports that tested off-edge initializations stall near 0.1 accuracy as depth increases, whereas edge-of-chaos initialization improves learning.
relationships.display_finding: Edge-of-chaos initialization improved learning, whereas tested off-edge initializations stalled near 0.1 accuracy as depth increased.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MNIST experiments comparing initialization and activation effects on learning
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports better learning behavior for edge-of-chaos initialization and faster or higher accuracy for selected activation/depth settings (R1–R8, R10, R12, R14, R16, R22, R24). These are accuracy results, not training-error measurements.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: small width with depth greater than width, and ReLU versus Swish comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Swish does not uniformly outperform ReLU: ReLU has slightly higher reported validation accuracy at width 5/depth 10 and width 10/depth 20, while the text qualifies the Swish advantage by architecture (R17–R20).
